fixed.title: PRODUCT MONOGRAPH INCLUDING PATIENT MEDICATION INFORMATION

blocks.text: OSTREVIA (lumiravostat) is indicated for the treatment of adults with moderate to severe chronic hand eczema that has not responded adequately to potent topical corticosteroids, or when these are not advisable.
Pediatrics (< 18 years of age): No data are available to Health Canada; therefore, Health Canada has not authorized an indication for pediatric use.
Geriatrics (≥ 65 years of age): Clinical studies included too few patients aged 65 and over to determine whether they respond differently. Use with caution.

items: Patients who are hypersensitive to lumiravostat or to any ingredient in the formulation, including any non-medicinal ingredient. For a complete listing, see 6 DOSAGE FORMS, STRENGTHS, COMPOSITION, AND PACKAGING.
Patients with active tuberculosis or an active serious infection.

blocks.text:
Serious Warnings and Precautions
• Serious infections leading to hospitalization or death, including tuberculosis, have occurred (see 7 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, Immune).
• Malignancies, including lymphoma, have occurred (see 7 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, Carcinogenesis and Genotoxicity).
• Thrombosis, including pulmonary embolism, has occurred (see 7 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, Hematologic).
Screen for latent tuberculosis and check blood counts and liver enzymes before starting treatment (see 7 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS).
The recommended dose is 10 mg once daily, with or without food. The dose may be increased to 25 mg once daily if the response is inadequate after 12 weeks.
Moderate hepatic impairment: 10 mg once daily. Severe hepatic impairment: not recommended.
With strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (for example ketoconazole or clarithromycin): 10 mg once daily.
Renal impairment: no dose adjustment.
Swallow tablets whole with water, with or without food.
If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible unless the next dose is due within 12 hours. Do not take two doses at once.
There is no specific antidote. Monitor the patient for signs of adverse reactions and give supportive treatment. Lumiravostat is not removed by haemodialysis to a meaningful extent.
For management of a suspected drug overdose, contact your regional poison control centre.

rows: microcrystalline cellulose, mannitol, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate; film coat: hypromellose, titanium dioxide, macrogol (25 mg tablets also iron oxide yellow)

blocks.text: 10 mg: white, round, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "10" on the other.
25 mg: yellow, oval, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "25" on the other.
Blister packs of 30 tablets (3 x 10).
Please see 3 SERIOUS WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS BOX.

Carcinogenesis and Genotoxicity: Malignancy, including lymphoma and non-melanoma skin cancer, has been reported. Consider the risks and benefits before starting treatment in patients with a known malignancy.
Hematologic: Venous thromboembolism, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, has been reported. Use with caution in patients with risk factors and stop treatment if it occurs.
Hepatic/Biliary/Pancreatic: Elevations of liver enzymes have occurred. Interrupt treatment if drug-induced liver injury is suspected.

Immune: Serious infections, including tuberculosis, pneumonia, cellulitis and herpes zoster, have been reported, some leading to hospitalization or death. Screen patients for latent tuberculosis before starting treatment and treat it first. Interrupt treatment if a serious infection develops.
Monitoring and Laboratory Tests: Monitor lymphocyte and neutrophil counts, haemoglobin and liver enzymes at baseline, at 4 weeks and every 3 months.

Lumiravostat caused embryo-fetal toxicity in rats and rabbits. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose.
It is not known whether lumiravostat passes into human milk. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose.
Safety and efficacy have not been established.
Infections were more frequent in patients aged 65 and over.
The most common adverse reactions (≥ 10%) were nasopharyngitis. Serious infections, malignancy and thrombosis are described in 7 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS.

Clinical trials are conducted under very specific conditions. The adverse reaction rates observed in the clinical trials, therefore, may not reflect the rates observed in practice and should not be compared to the rates in the clinical trials of another drug.

rows: headache, nausea, acne, herpes zoster, lymphopenia, neutropenia, alanine aminotransferase increased

subs.title: Less Common Clinical Trial Adverse Reactions

blocks.text: Infections: pneumonia, cellulitis. Vascular: deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism.
Hypersensitivity reactions, including angioedema, have been reported.
Lumiravostat is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase lumiravostat exposure (use 10 mg once daily). Strong CYP3A4 inducers, such as rifampicin, reduce exposure; avoid concomitant use.
Food does not affect exposure to a clinically relevant extent.
St. John's wort is a CYP3A4 inducer and may reduce exposure; avoid.
Interactions with laboratory tests have not been established.
Lumiravostat is a reversible inhibitor of the fictional STRK1 kinase, which signals downstream of several cytokines involved in skin inflammation.
Dose-dependent reductions in markers of skin inflammation were seen within 2 weeks.
Peak plasma concentrations are reached 1 to 2 hours after a dose. The half-life is about 16 hours. Lumiravostat is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4.
Store at 15°C to 30°C. Keep in the original package to protect from moisture. Keep out of reach and sight of children.
Proper name: lumiravostat. Molecular formula and mass: fictional. Physicochemical properties: white to off-white powder, slightly soluble in water.

In two 16-week placebo-controlled studies (fictional HANDS-1 and HANDS-2, 1,210 adults), 38% of patients on lumiravostat 25 mg and 31% on 10 mg reached clear or almost clear hands, against 12% on placebo.
Lumiravostat was not genotoxic. Embryo-fetal toxicity was seen in rats and rabbits at exposures close to the human exposure at 25 mg.

blocks.text:
Serious Warnings and Precautions
• Serious infections: OSTREVIA can lower your ability to fight infections. Some infections, including tuberculosis, have led to hospital stays or death.
• Cancer: some people taking OSTREVIA have had cancers, including lymphoma.
• Blood clots: blood clots in the legs or lungs have happened and can be life-threatening.
OSTREVIA is used in adults to treat moderate to severe hand eczema that has not got better with strong steroid creams, or when those creams are not suitable.
OSTREVIA blocks a protein in the body that drives inflammation in the skin. This helps reduce redness, itching and cracking.
Medicinal ingredient: lumiravostat.
Non-medicinal ingredients: microcrystalline cellulose, mannitol, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate; film coat: hypromellose, titanium dioxide, macrogol (25 mg tablets also iron oxide yellow).

blocks.text: This includes any drugs, vitamins, minerals, natural supplements or alternative medicines.

sections.title: The following may interact with OSTREVIA

items: medicines for fungal infections such as ketoconazole

blocks.text: Take OSTREVIA exactly as your healthcare professional tells you. Swallow the tablet whole with water, with or without food.
Adults: one 10 mg tablet once a day. Your healthcare professional may increase this to 25 mg once a day after 12 weeks.

If you think you, or a person you are caring for, have taken too much OSTREVIA, contact a healthcare professional, hospital emergency department, regional poison control centre or Health Canada's toll-free number, 1-844 POISON-X (1-844-764-7669) immediately, even if there are no signs or symptoms.
If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If your next dose is due within 12 hours, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses at once.

sections.title: Possible side effects from using OSTREVIA

blocks.text: These are not all the possible side effects. If you have any side effects not listed here, tell your healthcare professional.

items: runny or stuffy nose, sore throat

sections.title: Serious side effects and what to do about them

rows: Infection: fever, cough, chills, burning when you pass urine
Blood clot: swelling or pain in one leg, sudden chest pain or shortness of breath
Stop taking the drug and get immediate medical help

blocks.text: You can report any suspected side effects associated with the use of health products to Health Canada by: visiting the web page on Adverse Reaction Reporting for information on how to report online, by mail or by fax; or calling toll-free at 1-866-234-2345. NOTE: Contact your healthcare professional if you need information about how to manage your side effects. The Canada Vigilance Program does not provide medical advice.
Store at 15°C to 30°C in the original package to protect from moisture. Keep out of reach and sight of children.
